items.stem: What is the strongest form for a chart title in a data story?

options.text: A short insight statement that says what the chart means
options.rationale: Correct: insight titles tell the reader the takeaway directly.

options.text: The name of the metric and date range only
options.rationale: A label leaves the reader to infer the point.
An unanswered question does not convey the message.

options.text: No title, to keep the slide clean
options.rationale: Without a title the audience may miss the point.

items.explanation: Correct: insight titles tell the reader the takeaway directly.

items.stem: Which TWO choices present data honestly? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Start a bar chart's value axis at zero
options.rationale: Correct: a zero baseline avoids exaggerating differences in bar length.

options.text: Show an uncertainty range alongside a point estimate
options.rationale: Correct: showing uncertainty prevents overstating precision.

options.text: Choose the time window that makes the trend look best
options.rationale: Cherry-picking the window misleads the audience.

options.text: Use a dual axis to make two unrelated series appear correlated
options.rationale: Dual axes can manufacture a false visual relationship.

items.explanation: Correct: a zero baseline avoids exaggerating differences in bar length.

items.stem: An executive has two minutes. What should the data story lead with?

options.text: The single key message and its recommendation
options.rationale: Correct: lead with the message the decision needs.

options.text: The data collection methodology in full
options.rationale: Method detail buries the message for a busy executive.

options.text: Every chart produced during the analysis

options.rationale: A glossary delays the message the audience needs.

items.explanation: Correct: lead with the message the decision needs.
